items.title: Beyoncé Makes History As First Artist With 100 Grammy Nominations
items.summary:
Beyoncé passed a major milestone on Monday morning (Nov. 16) when she became the first artist in history to land 100 lifetime Grammy nominations. When the full list for the 2027 nominees was announced, Queen Bey found herself crossing into historic territory when the B’Day 20th anniversary reissue bonus track, “Morning Dew (Donk),” snagged a nomination for best R&B solo performance.

The previously unreleased song that was released on July 4 was co-written by Bey, Pharrell Williams, The-Dream and Darius Dixon and produced by the singer and Pharrell. It will face competition in the best R&B solo performance category from Kehlani (“Out the Window”), Victoria Monét (“Let Me”), Jill Scott (“Pressha”) and Tems (“What You Need”).

In addition to be the most-awarded artist in Grammy history with 35 wins to date — surpassing late conductor Georg Solti’s 32 Grammys — Beyoncé is well ahead in the most-nominations category, safely in front of husband Jay-Z at 89 (with 25 wins), Paul McCartney at 86 (with 19 wins), producer Quincy Jones at 80 (with 28 wins) and Star Wars composer John Williams at 79 (with 27 wins). Queen Bey also set the high bar for most nominations in a year she she earned 11 noms for her Cowboy Carter album at the 2025 Grammy Awards. Her three wins at the 2025 Grammys boosted her total to date to 35, making her the most-honored Grammy winner ever, among female musicians and all artists overall.

In 2025, Cowboy Carter also early Beyoncé her first album of the year win, as well as her first best country album trophy.

This year’s Grammy nominees are led by RAYE, who…
items.t: Beyoncé Makes History As First Artist With 100 Grammy Nominations

items.title: Rosalía, Shakira & More: These Are the Latino Artists Nominated for the 2027 Grammys
items.summary:
Less than a week after emerging as one of the biggest winners at the Latin Grammys, Rosalía is making history at the Grammys as one of the most nominated artists for the 2027 edition. The Spanish superstar received nine nominations on Monday (Nov. 16) for her acclaimed LUX , including album of the year, as well as song of the year and record of the year for “Berghain” featuring Björk and Yves Tumor.

She becomes the the first Hispanic woman and the second Latin artist to achieve this milestone, following Bad Bunny, who last year became the first to be nominated in all three major categories. The Puerto Rican superstar went on to win the night’s top honor, album of the year, for DeBÍ TiRAR MáS FOToS , a victory that mirrored his Latin Grammy victory in the same category. Last Thursday, Rosalía also won that latter accolade for LUX (as well as song of the year for “La Perla” featuring Yahritza y Su Esencia).

items.title: Morgan Wallen, Garth Brooks, Taylor Swift & More Artists With Most Weeks at No. 1 on Top Country Albums Chart: Full List
items.summary:
Morgan Wallen ’s I’m the Problem leads Billboard ‘s Top Country Albums chart (dated Nov. 21) for the 53rd nonconsecutive week. This ups Wallen’s career tally of weeks at No. 1 to 239, allowing him to extend his lead as the artist with the most weeks at No. 1 in the chart’s 62-year history.

Wallen’s achievement is especially impressive because he has amassed this hefty total of weeks at No. 1 in such a short amount of time. He first topped the chart a little more than six years ago — on Aug. 15, 2020.

I’m the Problem is Wallen’s third album to log a full year at No. 1 on Top Country Albums. Dangerous: The Double Album clung to the top spot for 97 weeks from 2021-23. One Thing at a Time led for 87 weeks from 2023-25. No other artist has spent 52 weeks on top with one album, much less three.

Top Country Albums originated as Hot Country Albums in the Jan. 11, 1964 issue of Billboard . Johnny Cash ’s Ring of Fire (The Best of Johnny Cash) headed the inaugural chart. The compilation was well-timed: “Ring of Fire” had headed Hot Country Songs for seven weeks the previous summer and had crossed over to reach the top 20 on the Billboard Hot 100.

The chart was named Hot Country LP’s from 1968 to 1984, when vinyl LPs were king.

Twenty-one artists have logged 50 or more weeks at No. 1 on Top Country Albums. Male solo artists dominate, as you might expect, though three female solo artists have achieved the feat, as have two groups. (One of those groups is an all-female group.) Only one Black artist has amassed 50 or more weeks at No. 1, though that may change as country becomes…
items.t: Morgan Wallen, Garth Brooks, Taylor Swift & More Artists With Most Weeks at No. 1 on Top Country Albums Chart: Full List

Released in July via Dim Mak Records, the song reaches the summit thanks to a 20% increase in plays at the format in the Nov. 6-12 tracking week, according to Luminate. The Dance Airplay chart measures songs’ weekly plays, as tabulated by Mediabase and provided to Billboard by Luminate, on a panel of dance-formatted radio stations in the United States.

“Gravity” also earns Ely Oaks his first Dance Airplay No. 1 and SACHA, her second, after “Set Me Free” with Armin van Buuren in January.

Aoki first appeared on Dance Airplay in April 2010 with “I’m in the House,” featuring Zuper Blahq (a pseudonym of will.i.am). He has since earned nine top 10s.

items.title: Dominic Fike Earns His Second Alternative Airplay No. 1 With ‘Babydoll’
items.summary:
Dominic Fike scores his second No. 1 on Billboard ’s Alternative Airplay chart (dated Nov. 21) as “Babydoll” rises two spots.

Fike first topped the chart in 2019 with his breakthrough single, “3 Nights.” He returned to the list once after that, before “Babydoll,” with “Chicken Tenders” (No. 34 peak in 2020). Both of his leaders come from the same project: “Babydoll” and “3 Nights” were each introduced on his 2018 EP, Don’t Forget About Me, Demos , the project that preceded his three studio albums.

“Babydoll” found a new audience in early 2026 when it became a popular sound on TikTok, eight years after its original release. The song was then newly promoted, along with 2025 track “White Keys.”

The run of “Babydoll” at alternative radio accompanies its broader success. Earlier this month, “Babydoll” became Fike’s first No. 1 on Pop Airplay. In October, it reached No. 10 on the multimetric Billboard Hot 100 , giving Fike his first top 10. It was also a top three hit on both the Billboard Global 200 and the Billboard Global Excl. U.S. charts in April. (“White Keys” hit No. 32 on the Hot 100 the same month.)

“Babydoll,” released via Sandy Boys/Columbia/Legacy, is the second Alternative Airplay No. 1 for Columbia Records in 2026, following Tame Impala’s “Dracula” in February.

The Alternative Airplay chart measures songs’ weekly plays, as tabulated by Mediabase and provided to Billboard by Luminate, on 60 U.S. alternative radio stations. “Babydoll” hits No. 1 with support on stations including WTBV Tampa, Fla.; KYRK Corpus Christi, Texas; and KRAT Reno, Nev.

items.title: ASCAP Names Samantha Saturn as General Manager, ASCAP Nashville
items.summary:
The American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers (ASCAP) has appointed music executive and Nashville native Samantha Saturn as general manager, ASCAP Nashville, effective Dec. 1, 2026.

In the newly established role, Saturn will direct day-to-day operations in the Nashville office. She will dual-report directly to ASCAP chief operating officer and chief financial officer Brian Roberts and executive vp and head of creative membership Nicole George-Middleton , both based in ASCAP’s New York City headquarters.

Related

CL Signs With THEBLACKLABEL, Reuniting With Longtime Producer Teddy For 'Full Circle' Moment 

Severe Weather, Radius Clauses and Finding the Next Generation of Festival Headliners: 'It's a Year-by-Year Fight to Stay Alive' 

Most recently, Saturn served for nearly eight years as chief marketing officer of SESAC Music Group, leading global brand strategy, corporate communications, affiliate engagement and digital licensing modernization across multiple entities.

Saturn’s career has also included time at Columbia Records as senior vp of digital marketing, where she built digital sales and marketing platforms for artists including Adele, The Chicks, Beyoncé, John Legend, AC/DC, Bruce Springsteen and more. She is an alumna of Leadership Music (Class of 2024) and a former board member at Gilda’s Club of Middle Tennessee and Watkins College of Art at Belmont University.

items.title: Jesús López  Steps Down as Head of Universal Music Latin America/Iberian Penninsula, Named Chairman Emeritus of UMG’s Global Talent Services
items.summary:
Jesús López , the longtime head of Universal Music’s entire Latin music business and one of the most iconic and influential executives in Latin music, will step down from his longtime position as chairman/CEO of Universal Music Latin America/Iberian Penninsula, Billboard can officially announce.

López will take on a new role as chairman emeritus for Global Talent Services (GTS), the UMG artist management, booking, promotion and services company that he launched in 2007 and which today has offices in eight countries. In his new capacity, he will continue to provide his longtime expertise and knowledge of the Spanish-language music market and its artists. Narcis Rebollo will remain as president/CEO of GTS.

items.title: The Alternative Number Ones: Fastball’s “The Way”

This column is a companion piece to  The Number Ones . The column is now biweekly, alternating with The Number Ones on Mondays. 

Dig, if you will, the late-'90s cool-guy uniform. The shiny thrift-shop button-up with the top three buttons open — sometimes neon green, sometimes loud-ass paisley, often with a butterfly collar popped onto the outside of your peacoat. items.title: Watch U2’s surprise opening performance to kick off 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony
items.summary:
U2 made a surprise appearance at the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony, opening the night with a live performance.

READ MORE: U2: “You have to up your game when people step into the room like Fontaines D.C.” 

The ceremony took place at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles on Saturday night (November 14), and saw Oasis , Billy Idol , Iron Maiden , Joy Division / New Order , Sade , Luther Vandross , Phil Collins and Wu-Tang Clan inducted into the Rock Hall .

As usual, there were a huge number of guest appearances across the night, including Jack Black, St. Vincent, Metallica, Rage Against The Machine and Mötley Crüe celebrating Iron Maiden, Bob Odenkirk and Stephen Wilson Jr. there for Oasis, and Deftones , Chvrches ‘ Lauren Mayberry and Peter Hook joining forces to perform two Joy Division and New Order classics .

One of the most unexpected moments of the night, however, came when U2 came out to open the ceremony, playing two songs.

The band were inducted back in 2005 for the Rock Hall – the same year that they were made eligible – and took to the stage over the weekend to play ‘Silencio’, a new single from their recently released album ‘ Carnaval De Luz ’ which they performed backed by a police riot force, as well as the classic ‘Pride (In the Name of Love)’.

Also on the night, Phil Collins also delivered an emotional acceptance speech after Cynthia Erivo performed ‘In The Air Tonight’ accompanied by Blink-182 ‘s Travis Barker on drums, and Gwen Stefani joined Billy Idol on stage.

items.title: Muse bring a singing robot and ‘The Wow! Signal’ to The O2 in London
items.summary:
Muse played the first of two London dates last night (Sunday November 15), bringing the universe of ‘ The Wow! Signal ‘ to The O2 with a singing robot and an epic new stage show. Check out photos, footage and the setlist below.

READ MORE: Matt Bellamy on rediscovering his own muse: “I can’t live without music – that feeling came back to me on this album” 

The Devonshire space rock trio kicked off their new run and debuted their huge new production in Manchester last week, ahead of their two-night residency in the capital.

The show began with the screens taking the crowd back to August 15, 1977 – the date that a powerful, unexplained 72-second radio burst was detected, originating from the constellation Sagittarius and with its bandwidth and intensity suggesting a possible extraterrestrial source. It became known as ‘The Wow! Signal’. The gig was introduced by frontman Matt Bellamy emerging from floating hexagonal b-stage with laser lights surrounding him for new album highlight ‘Hexagons’, before rejoining his bandmates for the metal-tinged ‘The Sickness In You And I’ and ‘Unravelling’.

The band performed below a giant 3D representation of ‘The Wow! Signal’ waveform forming in space, also seen on the album artwork, and in front of a scene depicting one of Jupiter’s moons, Europa.

Fans’ eyes were drawn to the AI robot stood at the back of the standing area, appearing to be manning a sound desk. It has been shared that the robot’s name is Ameca, and is now a curious fixture of the show for regularly adjusting controls as well as singing vocals on a reimagined version of…

items.title: Justice’s ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ score will be the only video game soundtrack the band ever do
items.summary:
Justice have said that their score for Grand Theft Auto 6 will be the only video game soundtrack they ever do.

READ MORE: Every song confirmed for the ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ soundtrack so far 

Last month, Rockstar Games confirmed that dance titans Justice had composed an original score for Grand Theft Auto 6 . So far, two songs from the project have been released –  ‘Flower In A Hurricane’, which features Tame Impala , SZA and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard , and Gesaffelstein collab ‘Pusher’.

The fifty-track, three hour collection will be available to stream December 11 and the record will also be getting a physical release, with a range of vinyl available to pre-order now.

Before that, fans will be able to hear Justice’s music later this week (November 19) when Grand Theft Auto 6 finally releases.

In a new interview with French publication Rockyrama , Justice’s Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay have spoken about their decision to work on the highly-anticipated video game.

“When [the offer] arrived on the table, we thought : “If there’s one video game we have to do, it’s this one.” As soon as we accepted and started working [on it], we thought it would probably be the first and last score we’ll ever do for a video game,” they said.

According to the band, Rockstar weren’t looking for a specific type of sound or music style for the Grand Theft Auto 6 score. “but rather the emotion that the music should give the player at specific moments.”

They went on to call their Grand Theft Auto 6 score a “special project” but confirmed that they consider it a “real” Justice…
items.t: Justice’s ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ score will be the only video game soundtrack the band ever do

items.summary:
Jack Black and St. Vincent performed with members of Metallica , Rage Against The Machine and Mötley Crüe  for a one-off performance at the Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame – celebrating Iron Maiden being inducted.

READ MORE: Iron Maiden – ‘Senjutsu’ review: an imaginative instant classic 

The British heavy metal icons were finally inducted into the Rock Hall, having formed back in 1975 and been eligible since 2005 – 25 years after their first significant release.

While they weren’t there in person to attend the ceremony on Saturday (November 14) due to touring commitments in Australia, there was a special supergroup that performed at the event to celebrate their huge impact on the metal and rock world.

Jack Black and St. Vincent, came out to perform classic Maiden track ‘The Trooper’, backed by Metallica members Kirk Hammett and Robert Trujillo, Mötley Crüe guitarist John 5, and Rage Against the Machine’s Brad Wilk.

The supergroup was dubbed ‘St. RageTallica 5’, and put their own distinctive spin on the 1983 classic, which was released as part of their fourth studio album, ‘Piece of Mind’. Check it out below.

Jack Black was also on hand to induct the band on the night, sharing a speech on stage and saying: “Has there ever been a band that has rocked this hard for this long? The answer is ‘no.’

“In fact, they’re not even here tonight because they’re rocking half way around the world.”

When it was announced that they were being inducted, the band’s manager shared a statement on their behalf sharing their gratitude. “We’d like to thank the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame for…

items.title: Johnny Depp’s Hollywood return ‘Ebenezer’ hits top of box office
items.summary:
Johnny Depp ’s Ebenezer is a box office hit despite middling reviews from critics.

Director Ti West’s new take on Charles Dickens’ classic novella A Christmas Carol sees Depp take on the role of Ebenezer Scrooge with Ian McKellen, Rupert Grint and Daisy Ridley also starring.

Ebenezer hit cinemas on Friday (November 13) and across its opening weekend, took a reported $42million worldwide, making it the number one film at the box office. It was the most popular film in UK cinemas, taking $5.4million. Ebenezer also topped the box office in Italy, Mexico, Spain, Poland, Belgium and Central America (via Variety ).

Ahead of its release, Ebenezer received middling reviews from critics and currently has a Rotten Tomatoes score of just 54 per cent. However the response from movie goers has been a lot more positive with Ebenezer racking up a 90 per cent score on the review aggregate site’s fan-voted ‘Popcornmeter’.

Ebenezer is also Johnny Depp’s first major studio movie since 2018’s Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes Of Grindelwald. The same year the Harry Potter prequel was released, Depp’s ex-wife Amber Heard wrote an op-ed for The Washington Post in which she alleged she was domestically abused by the actor

Two years later, Depp lost a libel case in the UK against The Sun for referring to him as a “wife beater” in their reporting and he was asked to resign from the Fantastic Beasts franchise by studio bosses. items.title: Peter Hook tells Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame why New Order will never get back together (without Oasis reunion money)
items.summary:
Peter Hook has shut down hopes of a New Order reunion while at the Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame, and said that it would have to be an amount of money similar to what Oasis were offered to make him reconsider.

READ MORE: “It felt like we were changing the world”: inside New Order’s seminal ‘Power, Corruption & Lies’ 

The bassist attended the Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame ceremony on Saturday (November 14) as Joy Division and New Order were inducted together. He appeared at the event without any of the other bandmates present, and performed ‘Love Will Tear Us Apart’ and ‘Bizarre Love Triangle’ alongside Deftones and Chvrches .

Stephen Morris and Gillian Gilbert both did not attend due to health reasons, with Gilbert battling cancer.   Bernard Sumner did not show up on the night either.

Hook played with Joy Division until they became New Order when Ian Curtis took his own life in 1980, before parting ways with the band in 2007 – leading to years of legal battle and trading barbs. There was longstanding tension between some of the other members when he left the band, and he also cited dissatisfaction about the creative direction of the band when he left. New Order went on to tour and record without the bassist, while Peter Hook & The Light have spent years touring to celebrate the discographies of both bands.

items.title: Russell Brand still maintains innocence via statement read by wife on podcast
items.summary:
Russell Brand has shared a statement from jail that says he is innocent of rape and sexual assault.

Last week (November 9), Brand was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison after being found guilty of rape and three counts of sexual assault . During the trial, he was acquitted of two other rape charges and an attempted indecent assault. Throughout the trial, he denied the accusations, saying the incidents had either been consensual, reinvented or re-imagined.

Over the weekend, Brand’s wife Laura Gallacher shared a statement from Brand via the couple’s weekly podcast Sunday Service where the comedian maintains his innocence.

“Beloved brothers and sisters in Christ, God bless you for your support. As you know, I am not guilty for the offences I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening. The good news is that Christ is with us when we choose him, and I do,” Brand said via Gallacher.

He confirmed that he had been moved to HMP Littlehey, “the biggest sex offenders’ prison in Europe”, but had found the staff “strong, kind, and dedicated.”

“And as for my fellow prisoners, I now know that I am in no position to judge anyone,” he continued. “I don’t know which other men here are not guilty, and the ones that are, they are people that Christ died to save, like you and me, let us all love, pray for, and forgive one another as God forgave us.”

Following his conviction, Brand’s former girlfriend Jemima Goldsmith accused him of “violence, coercive control and abuse” while the Met Police have confirmed they’re investigating two more rape allegations against…
items.t: Russell Brand still maintains innocence via statement read by wife on podcast

items.title: ‘I have to sell my bum on OnlyFans to go on tour’: Kate Nash on fame, feminism and fighting the music business
items.summary:
She threw a (metaphorical) brick through Spotify’s window and exposed industry failings with her ‘Butts for Tour Buses’ campaign. Now the singer is embracing her Irish roots with her new album’s fighting spirit

Kate Nash was standing on a fire truck in a showgirl outfit complete with white tights and pink G-string, shouting through a loudhailer about the music industry’s failure to pay artists fairly, when she wondered if she’d gone too far. It was 2024 and the truck, which made pit stops outside the London offices of Spotify and Live Nation, had a large black-and-white picture of Nash’s bum on the back along with the words “Butts for Tour Buses” – a reference to her newly launched OnlyFans account, which she was using to fund her tour.

That afternoon, she called her manager Kat. “I told her: ‘I’ve thrown a brick through the window at Spotify.’ She went: ‘What, literally?’ and I said: ‘No, but I’ve been standing outside their offices with a megaphone, so that relationship is over. I don’t think we’ll be making their New Music Friday feature.’ And we didn’t.”

items.title: ‘A songbook for protest movements’: how did this secret mission to smuggle antifascist music out of Spain ever get forgotten?
items.summary:
In 1961, a group of Italian creatives crossed the border to collect anti-Franco resistance songs and share them with the world – sparking intense backlash from the dictator. A new documentary retraces that perilous journey

In the summer of 1961, four Italians crossed the Pyrenees into fascist Spain. Unknown to the border guards, their car was loaded with microfilm, a tape recorder and, tucked in the pocket of a writer and musician named Sergio Liberovici, a book of matches – each split in half, etched with the addresses of Spanish antifascists in miniature and glued back together, a hairline fracture concealing secrets that, if discovered, could result in jail or worse.

Along with Michele Luciano Straniero, Emilio Jona and Margherita Galante Garrone, Liberovici was a member of a leftwing collective named Cantacronache. Formed in 1958 and counting Italo Calvino and Umberto Eco among their collaborators, the collective was repulsed by the superficiality of Italian pop music and hoped to revitalise culture with Brechtian realism. At the time, Italy was fiercely divided into leftwing and rightwing political camps, and it was a record label, Italia Canta, linked to the Italian Communist party, that financed the trip. Its goal: to secretly document the resistance songs of the anti-Franco underground. It was a perilous task for all involved, but especially so for Cantacronache’s contacts.

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘A songbook for protest movements’: how did this secret mission to smuggle antifascist music out of Spain ever get forgotten?

items.title: Ocean Colour Scene review – no other band of their era can do it like this
items.summary:
Ulster Hall, Belfast
With two sets of fathers and sons now in the group, as they play all of Moseley Shoals on its 30th anniversary, the indie stalwarts have aged into seismic and soulful performers

‘It’s only 30 years ago,” Simon Fowler says of Moseley Shoals. He would seem to mean it, but 30 years makes Ocean Colour Scene’s breakthrough album as old now as Revolver was when they were making it. The band once derided for raiding the 60s are now heritage themselves. They open the album’s anniversary tour on the stage where Led Zeppelin first played Stairway to Heaven, and you can’t help but appreciate the lineage.

They walk on to Green Onions, fresh from the Crown Bar, and open with You’ve Got It Bad, all supreme Motown stomp. Fowler sings with a hand in his pocket and looks taken aback by the welcome. The casualness is a conduit: his voice has aged into something close to peak Joe Cocker, grained at the edges, honey underneath. Lining Your Pockets is more resounding than ever.

items.title: Paris Paloma review – arena-scale alt-pop drama from a singer on her way to bigger things
items.summary:
Bristol Beacon
The UK artist combines feminist fury with accessible melodies and a dramatic flair that sees her alternately pogoing and seeking out the wind machines at the prow of the stage

People are dancing to a song they don’t know, with flower garlands in their hair and their arms around their friends. This reaction to Fairy Dance, an unreleased track written about the community that has sprung up around her music, says a lot about the moment Paris Paloma finds herself in, and tonight’s show feels for all the world like a stepping stone to bigger things.

Throughout, Paloma leans in to the built-in drama of songs from her second album, The Fatal Flaw, which pairs ornate folk arrangements with the sort of arena-sized alt-pop production favoured by Florence + the Machine. With a sculpture inspired by surrealist Ithell Colquhoun’s Tree of Veins dominating the stage, she falls to her knees to deliver high notes and seeks out wind machines at the prow of the stage, her flowing crimson dress buffeted as if on a wintry moor.

items.title: Philippines’ Carmelle wins first Eurovision contest in Asia
items.summary:
Filipino entry, pop and rap song Sobra-Sobra, takes 19-year-old to victory at grand final in Bangkok

Carmelle Collado has won the first Eurovision song contest Asia, taking the Philippines’ entry, Sobra-Sobra, to victory in Bangkok on Saturday night, at the first regional edition of the contest to be staged outside Europe.

Eleven countries competed at the One Bangkok Forum in central Bangkok, and the show ran for two and a half hours including advertising.
